title: Card or cash for tickets?
hook: Would changing the payment method change your maximum bid?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare willingness to pay under payment methods while holding the ticket fixed.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare willingness to pay under payment methods while holding the ticket fixed.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: The same toy ticket costs €40 with no payment fee. How much does paying by card cost if it adds a €2 fee? Toy inputs A=[40, 2]; B=[40, 0].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[42, 40, 2], [40, 40, 0]]. Labels: Total €, Ticket €, Fee €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The ticket is held fixed while the fee changes the cash total. If fees were also identical, this budget calculation would be identical across methods. Reported willingness to pay is a separate empirical quantity.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Ticket €=40, Payment fee €=0. What is Total €? Answer: 40.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Ticket €=40, Payment fee €=0. What is Total €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 40. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: MBA students bid up to twice as much for Celtics tickets when paying by credit card instead of cash (Prelec & Simester, 2001).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare willingness to pay under payment methods while holding the ticket fixed.
